title: A co-tenant workload steals host CPU: services wait on the runqueue, not on I/O

problem.summary: An unrelated workload sharing the host consumes CPU. Application services are never themselves busy, but each time they become ready to run they wait measurably longer before a CPU actually runs them. User-facing latency moves only slightly, so dashboards look nearly normal; the delay is only visible in the scheduler.
symptoms: mild, intermittent latency jitter across several unrelated services at once
no service is itself busy: per-container CPU is flat or falling
no new error signatures; requests still succeed
host CPU busy rises but is not exhausted, and host load rises moderately

discriminators.signal: runqueue delay: time from sched_waking to the sched_switch that runs the thread
discriminators.this_problem: p95 runqueue delay inflates several-fold across MANY unrelated processes at once, with the busiest application process among the worst
discriminators.not_this_problem: runqueue delay is flat or falls; the median across processes stays at or below 1x
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED from raw L0 via babeltrace2. Co-tenant run: node p95 0.034 -> 0.242 ms = 7.12x (n=48,886); median 1.78x across 52 high-volume processes. CONTROL, slow-datastore run: max 1.59x, median 0.84x, and node 0.97x. See evidence/L0_runqueue_delay_cotenant.json and evidence/L0_runqueue_delay_CONTROL_slowdb.json

discriminators.signal: blocking-syscall duration of the same processes
discriminators.this_problem: syscall durations stay flat: nothing is blocking longer, the threads simply cannot get a CPU
discriminators.not_this_problem: one component's blocking syscall inflates by an order of magnitude
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED: on the co-tenant run the datastore's poll p95 went 16.6 -> 18.7 ms = 1.12x (n=45,337) and the largest inflation of ANY syscall was 1.8x. On the slow-datastore run the same syscall on the same component was 36.83x. See evidence/L0_blocking_syscall_CONTROL_cotenant.json

discriminators.this_problem: no component has slow incoming edges; the slowdown does not converge anywhere
discriminators.not_this_problem: slow edges converge on one component
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED: edge_convergence.py returns converged_on = null on the co-tenant run, max edge slowdown 1.7x with zero edges over the 2x threshold. See evidence/L0_edge_convergence_CONTROL_cotenant.json

discriminators.this_problem: a container consumes steady CPU it did not consume in the baseline and has NO call-graph edges
discriminators.not_this_problem: the extra CPU belongs to a service that appears in the call graph
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED: the co-tenant consumed 2.00 cores against a 0.00 baseline with no call-path edges; host busy cores 5.31 -> 7.96 (x1.5), so the host retained headroom. See evidence/measured_verdict_noisy_neighbor_r1.json

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the delayed services show a raised runnable_wait share (ready to run, waiting for a CPU)
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: runnable_wait of the labelled culprit never exceeds 4% in ANY fault family (max 4.0% svc_mem_cap, 2.6% svc_cpu_cap); on the co-tenant run the highest runnable_wait across services was 1.6%. See evidence/wait_signature_all_families.json
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: removed from the discriminators. Do not reinstate without new evidence.
unverified_do_not_claim.agent_note: The share of wall time a service spends in a runnable state. Measured across every labelled fault: it never exceeds 4%, because that share is diluted by ordinary idle waiting. Use per-wakeup runqueue DELAY instead, which shows the effect clearly.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the wait decomposition of the culprit distinguishes this fault
unverified_do_not_claim.status: CANNOT BE MEASURED for this family
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: this fault is labelled against the host, and L2 produces no record for 'host'. Across 93 runs there is no culprit-side L2 record for anomaly_cpu, anomaly_disk, anomaly_mem, anomaly_net or noisy_neighbor.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: either derive a host-level L2 record, or accept that this family is diagnosed from metrics + topology only.
unverified_do_not_claim.agent_note: The wait decomposition of the culprit. For host-attributed faults no culprit-side wait record exists at all, so its absence is meaningless here.

reproduction.system: Sock Shop or Train Ticket on Ubuntu 24.04, LTTng 2.15, Docker 27+, single GCP n2 VM

traces: server span duration per service, only to confirm the impact is mild
collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Runqueue delay needs exactly two tracepoints: sched_waking gives the moment a thread became runnable, and sched_switch (next_tid) gives the moment a CPU actually ran it. The difference is the delay. Syscall events are collected only as the NEGATIVE control - showing durations stay flat is what separates this from a component blocked on I/O. Nothing else in the kernel trace is required.

processing.step: Stage the raw kernel trace (channels are stored gzipped)
processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata plus channel0_* streams. The metadata is CTF 2 (JSON preamble), so babeltrace 2.1 or newer is required; 2.0.x fails with an invalid-metadata error

processing.step: Measure runqueue delay per process, baseline window vs incident window
processing.expect: millions of wake->run pairs per window; a broad multi-process inflation of p95 indicates contention

processing.step: NEGATIVE CONTROL: confirm blocking-syscall durations did NOT inflate
processing.expect: no syscall inflates by more than about 2x; a 10x or larger inflation on one component means this is NOT the right blueprint

processing.step: Identify the off-call-path CPU consumer and emit the verdict
processing.expect: the top CPU consumer has no call-graph edges and was absent in the baseline

outputs.contains: culprit container, per-service runnable-wait share baseline versus incident, host CPU headroom
runnable-wait share per service over time, with the incident window shaded
which container took the CPU, which services waited, and why this is contention rather than saturation

verdict_when: p95 runqueue delay inflates several-fold across many unrelated processes
blocking-syscall durations stay flat over the same window
the slowdown does not converge on any single component in the call graph
a container with no call-graph role consumes CPU it did not consume in the baseline

rule_out.instead: a component waiting on I/O or a dependency
rule_out.when: one component's blocking syscall inflates by an order of magnitude while runqueue delay stays flat
host CPU is exhausted rather than merely raised, and user latency collapses instead of jittering

rule_out.instead: a service pinned by its own CPU limit
rule_out.when: only ONE service is delayed and it is on the call path

decision.root_cause_is: the co-tenant workload container itself, not any application service it delays

evidence_from_literature.claim: Runqueue delay separates CPU starvation from self-inflicted slowness better than utilisation does
evidence_from_literature.validated_on: our labelled co-tenant runs on both applications

provenance.notes: v3: rebuilt on the raw kernel trace read with babeltrace2, after the derived wait-share record was measured to be non-discriminative. Every discriminator now cites a measurement with its control. The decisive pair: runqueue delay 7.12x here vs 0.97x on the datastore fault, and the datastore's poll syscall 1.12x here vs 36.83x there - same signals, opposite directions.
